caption:
Everything that happened in the shipping industry in the last 24 hours (21 Nov 2026) 🚢

1. Brent ends week at $92.57 - third weekly loss
2. Tanker hit off Khasab - fire, crew safe
3. Bulker MIRO G grounds in France - 19 crew airlifted
4. Houthis threaten Jeddah - ships told to leave
5. Gunmen fire on bulker off Yemen - guards shoot back
6. Manila seeks warlike zone for Black Sea
7. US LNG exports hit 40 cargoes in a week
8. COSCO orders 16 VLCCs worth $2bn
9. Foresight orders 4 gas carriers at HD Hyundai

Sources are credited on each slide. Follow @jaimarineshorts for daily shipping news.

stories.headline: Brent ends week at [$92.57] - third weekly loss
stories.summary: Brent crude settled at $92.57 a barrel on Friday, 20 Nov, up 0.6% on the day, and December WTI closed at $83.98, up 0.9%. Reports of a tanker fire near Hormuz lifted prices. But Brent fell 3.4% over the week, its third weekly loss, as the IEA says global supply is back in surplus. OPEC+ meets on 29 Nov.

stories.headline: Tanker hit off Khasab - [fire, crew safe]
stories.summary: An outbound tanker was struck on its port bow by an unknown projectile on Friday, 20 Nov, about 8 nm north of Khasab, Oman, UKMTO said. A fire broke out, but no casualties or pollution were reported. Iran's IRGC claims the tanker hit a mine - not confirmed. Four tankers have been hit near Khasab in three days.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Jon Olav Eikenes / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

stories.headline: Bulker MIRO G grounds in France - [19 crew airlifted]
stories.summary: The Maltese-flagged bulk carrier MIRO G, 28,200 dwt, ran aground near Lit-et-Mixe in southwest France just after midnight on 20 Nov. Gusts of 48 knots dragged her anchor. An Air Force helicopter lifted 19 of the 22 crew to safety; the captain and two others stayed aboard. She has over 100 tonnes of diesel, but no pollution so far.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Ximonic (Simo Räsänen) / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

stories.headline: Houthis threaten Jeddah - [ships told to leave]
stories.summary: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said on 20 Nov that Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports will become targets if the Saudi-led coalition strikes Hodeidah. He urged shipping companies to move their ships away. The coalition says it has begun a targeted operation and hit Houthi capabilities at Hodeidah port. No attack on a Saudi port is confirmed.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · H. Zell / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)

stories.headline: Gunmen fire on bulker off Yemen - [guards shoot back]
stories.summary: Six armed men fired four shots at an eastbound bulk carrier about 95 nm southwest of Al Mukalla, Yemen, on Friday. The ship's security team fired warning shots and there were no injuries or damage. Orbital Risk Intelligence counted 15 attacks and piracy incidents worldwide in seven days - up 50% and the highest weekly total since mid-October.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Ian Kirk from Broadstone, Dorset, UK / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

stories.headline: Manila seeks [warlike zone] for Black Sea
stories.summary: The Philippines will seek an international review to declare the southwestern Black Sea a high-risk or warlike zone, Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said. It follows the suspected drone strike on LPG tanker Gas Husky, which sank off Bulgaria. All 19 Filipino crew were rescued by a Bulgarian helicopter; two had minor injuries. They await repatriation from Varna.

stories.headline: US LNG exports hit [40 cargoes] in a week
stories.summary: US LNG plants shipped 40 cargoes in the week to 18 Nov, up three from the week before, EIA data shows. LNG Prime says export capacity and ship departures both hit record highs. At the same time, Atlantic and Pacific spot LNG carrier rates fell for a second straight week, according to Spark Commodities.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · kremlin.ru website team / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)

stories.headline: COSCO orders [16 VLCCs] worth $2bn
stories.summary: COSCO Shipping Development has ordered 16 VLCCs of 307,000 dwt from China State Shipbuilding Group, worth CNY13.43 billion (US$2.01 billion), or about CNY839 million each. The methanol- and LNG-ready tankers will be built at Dalian Shipbuilding, with delivery from late 2029 to 2030.

stories.headline: Foresight orders [4 gas carriers] at HD Hyundai
stories.summary: UAE's Foresight Group has ordered four 90,000 cbm LPG/ammonia carriers from HD Hyundai Heavy Industries, worth an estimated US$470 million, for delivery in 2029-2030. They are the first of a planned 10-ship programme worth about $1.2 billion. Foresight runs seven VLGCs carrying US LPG for Indian state oil companies.
stories.photo_credit: Representative · Gordon Leggett / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
